what: PX-4 (2026-10-20): the native training step's transient values placed by their lifetimes (native_pack.place_by_lifetime) -- what the placement saves against the C plan's fixed spans, what it costs to make, what a run on the placed arena costs against a run on the C spans, and every placed run's gap to G26's alignment-aware concurrent-live bound -- on the 9.84M comparison decoder (vocabulary 260, width 384, 8 heads over 4 KV heads, 6 layers, FF 1024, tied; 8 sequences of 128 tokens) and the trace corpus's 356 placed pack runs.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 4 vCPUs: AVX-512F, no AVX512-BF16 and no AMX (the host PX-2b's records were made on), so the bf16 contract runs without its AMX and AVX512-BF16 instances; the ratios compare paths on this host only. gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, the library at -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno. Every cost record names the head it ran on (b6c50f1) and the first 16 hex digits of sha256(git diff HEAD -- runtime/c bcir): 6cc813b450351f77, this commit's runtime/c and bcir. Wall times are indicative: one virtualized host, one process at a time.

records.place.py: the cost driver: the K-step pack placed by lifetime (PLACES calls timed), the C plan's arenas, the placed arena and the bound, the model's figures at the decoder's other recompute sets and contracts (no run), then three trainers taking turns round by round -- c (the pack at the C spans, lending the C plan's arenas), c2 (the same again: the A/A control) and placed (the pack placed by lifetime, lending exactly the placement) -- each ratio's geometric mean and 95% Student-t interval, and every trainer's state
records.t4-bf16attnbf16.json: bf16+exp+reduce+attnbf16 at four threads: K 10, 24 rounds
records.t4-kblock.json: kblock+exp+reduce+attn (binary32) at four threads: K 10, 24 rounds
records.gaps.py: every placed pack run of the corpus row (native_decoder_fixtures.place_mismatch): its divergences and its extent's gap to the bound, with whether the exact search proved the layout optimal
records.gaps.json: gaps.py's run: the gap histogram in bytes

reading: Across the trace corpus's 356 placed runs the extent is G26's bound in 254 (each proved optimal by the bounded exact search) and 32 bytes above it (66 runs) or 52 bytes above it (36 runs) in the other 102, where the search stops at its budget without a proof; every placed run trains the C step's state and events bit for bit (train.plan.place.mismatch 0 of 356), none below its bound. On the 9.84M comparison decoder: no cost and no gain this host resolves for running on the placed arena -- placed / C spans x1.0022 (95% interval 0.987-1.018) under bf16 at four threads and x1.0086 (0.981-1.037) under binary32, beside A/A controls of x1.0107 (0.998-1.023) and x1.0193 (0.991-1.048); the ten-step pack placed in 123-166 ms (the median of 20 calls), its 1,640 (bf16) and 1,460 (binary32) transient values in 10 parts each, one a step, at 166,199,296 and 176,685,056 bytes against the C plan's 194,019,328 (0.857 and 0.911 of it), each at its bound, proved; the trainer's whole memory 355.9 -> 328.1 MB and 351.4 -> 334.1 MB; every trainer's state one state, bit for bit, over 24 rounds of 10-step calls. The placed arena against the C plan's at one step a call, by recompute set: binary32 0.911 (none), 0.878 (layers 0-2), 0.725 (all six); bf16 0.857 (none), 0.833 (layers 0-2), 0.725 (all six) -- each at its bound, proved.
witnesses: bcir/tests/test_native_place.py: the placement lawful and at its bound at the bench shape (every value placed once, aligned, its size and lifetime kept; no two live values sharing a byte; the plan verified under its laws; a value moved onto a live one refused by the codec and by the laws); the parts laid out apart; the bench row's placed arena; every placed run training the C step's bits (train.plan.place.mismatch); a placed trainer running only what it holds; the arguments outside the lent arenas; the comparison seeing each divergence; the fuzz harnesses holding their seeds to their verdicts (a replay build of each).
